application_fee.basis: Tamil Nadu Right to Information (Fees) Rules, 2005 (G.O. Ms. No. 989, Public (Estt. I & Leg.) Dept, 7 Oct 2005), r. 3(a), as amended; consolidated text corrected up to Nov 2018
application_fee.quote: shall be accompanied by an application fee of rupees ten
application_fee.note: The Oct 2005 notification said rupees fifty. TNSIC annual reports list the amending orders (G.O. Ms. No. 1012 of 20 Sep 2006, G.O. Ms. No. 72 P&AR of 20 Mar 2007, G.O. Ms. No. 12 P&AR of Jan 2011) and show rupees ten; the amending orders themselves were not found online, so the consolidated text is the source. No fee for a first or second appeal (TNSIC FAQ).

copy_fee_per_page.basis: Tamil Nadu Right to Information (Fees) Rules, 2005, r. 3(b)(i), as amended; consolidated text corrected up to Nov 2018
copy_fee_per_page.quote: rupees two for each page (in A-4 or A-3 size paper) created or copied
copy_fee_per_page.note: Larger paper is charged at actual cost (r. 3(b)(ii)). Inspection: no fee for the first hour, rupees five for every hour or fraction after (r. 3(b)(iv)). Further fees are paid by cash against receipt, demand draft or banker's cheque only (r. 3(b)).

bpl_certificate_required.basis: Government of Tamil Nadu RTI Online portal, FAQ on payment of the RTI fee (the exemption itself is RTI Act s. 7(5), proviso: see rti_act.json)
bpl_certificate_required.quote: no RTI fee is required to be paid by a citizen who is below poverty line ... the BPL applicant must attach a copy of the certificate issued by the appropriate government in this regard, along with the application
bpl_certificate_required.note: The Tamil Nadu Fees Rules, 2005 do not mention BPL, and no Tamil Nadu rule or G.O. on the proof was found, so this rests on the Government's own portal help text, which is not a rule. It mirrors central r. 5. The stricter reading (attach a copy of the certificate) is kept. A human should confirm it with the Public Department.

payment_modes.basis: Tamil Nadu Right to Information (Fees) Rules, 2005, r. 3(a), as amended; consolidated text corrected up to Nov 2018
payment_modes.quote: by cash or by affixing court fee stamp or by postal money order or by demand draft or bankers cheque payable in the head of account, as may be specified by the Public Authority
payment_modes.note: Statutory default for the application fee. The rule names a postal money order, not an Indian Postal Order (TNSIC says applications with postal orders were returned), and has no electronic mode. Further fees under s. 7(1) are cash, demand draft or banker's cheque only (r. 3(b)); court fee stamp and postal money order apply to the application fee alone. Not in r. 3(a): the Government also instructs payment into the State Treasury head of account against a challan (letter 19963/AR-III/2020-1 of 11 Dec 2020), and the online portal takes internet banking and debit card. The Madras High Court and the Legislative Assembly Secretariat have their own fee rules. Per-authority modes override this when the authority list exists.

filing_channels.basis: Government of Tamil Nadu RTI Online portal (rtionline.tn.gov.in); RTI Act 2005, s. 6(1) (in writing or electronic)
filing_channels.quote: Through this portal RTI application/first appeal can be filed by Indian Citizen only for the Departments/Public Authorities of the Government of Tamil Nadu ... the petitions and Appeals relating to the offices wherein this facility has not yet been implemented may be sent manually to those offices at present
filing_channels.note: The portal takes applications only for the Tamil Nadu departments and offices where the facility is implemented (Secretariat departments first); the central portal rtionline.gov.in does not take state authorities. Post and in person rest on s. 6(1) 'in writing' and the portal's 'manually'. The portal form holds 3000 characters; longer text goes in a PDF attachment.
